issues.description: The problem statement erroneously asks to "Create a `public class Lecture`" while the rest of the problem, the template code, and the solution all use the class name `Course`. This name mismatch inside the problem statement is a structural contradiction that can confuse students about the intended class name and which type they should implement.
issues.suggested_fix: Correct the problem statement so it consistently refers to the `Course` class (replace the mention of `Lecture` with `Course`). Alternatively, if the intended class name is `Lecture`, update the template and solution to use `Lecture` everywhere. Preferably keep `Course` to match existing template and solution.

issues.description: The problem statement (Part 1, Task 1) instructs students to "Create a `public class Lecture`" while the rest of the problem text, the initializer example, the template code and the solution all use the identifier `Course`. This inconsistent naming of the same conceptual entity (the course class) can confuse students when they try to map the textual requirement to the provided template and expected solution.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the naming consistent by updating the problem statement to refer to `Course` instead of `Lecture` (e.g. change "Create a `public class Lecture`" to "Create a `public class Course`"). This aligns the textual requirement with the template and solution and removes unnecessary confusion.
